title: AI fabrication suspected of writing dozens of articles in Canadian publications

reading.body:
This is a case of a fabricated identity used to place content in real publications, not a model error inside a single system. The byline, the headshot and the biography were synthetic, and the articles were accepted by editors who treated the persona as a freelance contributor. The failure sits at the point of commissioning and identity verification, upstream of publication.

The impersonation was sustained rather than incidental. The persona was used to advance a specific campaign against named individuals, and the harassment that followed reached a person whose only link was a business relationship. Catching it would have required verifying that a contributor exists independently of the text and image supplied, which the outlets did not do before publishing. One editor has acknowledged a vetting lapse.

What is not established is who operated the persona, whether the outlets knew or suspected anything, and whether the harassment was directed by the same party. The forensic finding that the headshot was AI-generated is a finding about the image, not a finding about intent.

reports.title: Exclusive—Fake AI columnist dupes Canadian press to target Moroccan dissidents, and a Turkish 'middleman'
Why we took down an article published under the name Daniel Robson
A statement on articles by ‘Daniel Robson’
Byline or bot? AI-generated ‘journalists’ start to appear in Canada
AI fabrication suspected of writing dozens of articles in Canadian publications

summary:
A fake AI-generated columnist named Daniel Robson infiltrated Canadian news outlets for nearly two years, publishing dozens of articles. The persona pushed narratives defending Morocco while targeting its critics, including Canadian-Moroccan businessman Hicham Jerando and former Moroccan intelligence officer Mehdi Hijaouy. Robson also attacked a Turkish textile seller named Fuat, whose only connection was doing business with Jerando. Fuat faced doxxing, threatening messages, and harassment from Morocco-based accounts, forcing him to seek psychiatric care and file a complaint in Istanbul.

After Türkiye Today investigated, forensic tools found Robson's headshot was 97 percent AI-generated. Canadian outlets including the Ottawa Citizen, Policy Options, and Western Standard removed his articles, though some acted only after being contacted. Policy Options editor Les Perreaux admitted a vetting lapse. Robson denied being fake and refused video calls. A retired colonel who included Robson in a book said he could not yet confirm Robson is real.
